text: Aveta is a Continental Celtic goddess. She is the goddess of the healing spring of Trier in Germany. The Romans depicted her as a nursing mother. This image suggests she was a tribal ancestor of the people who worshiped her. She is also shown holding baskets of fruit. The fruit points to her control over fertility. She appears in company with dogs. The Celts linked dogs to Otherworld and afterlife powers. Her healing spring was one of the many sacred waters venerated by the Continental Celts. These springs drew worshipers who sought cures for their ailments. Her attributes place her among the healing and fertility deities of the region. The images of Aveta come from votive offerings found at Trier. Her cult thus combines healing, fertility, and the powers of the afterlife.

okr.objective: This article establishes Aveta as the Continental Celtic goddess of the healing spring of Trier, depicted as a nursing mother with fruit and dogs.
